voice: A nervous, insinuating small-time fixer in the Peter Lorre tradition: ingratiating, evasive, unexpectedly precise, and rich in selective period underworld slang without phonetic gangster spelling.

entries.text: I thought it was a great year! I made a sawbuck on the Tunney-Dempsey fight in Philly!
Why are you showing me that?
All I know is somebody lifted the Egyptian pigsticker from the museum.
That's the new president of the Leyendecker Museum.
That's today's password. Also a very fine dance.
Crodfoller? He's an old pal of mine. What do you want to know?
The pigsticker? Somebody lifted it.
Those are the docks at the end of Twelfth Street.
The only Egyptian I know is an accountant named Rameses Najeer. He comes around sometimes and asks me riddles. I never know what to make of them.
Today Rameses asked me a two-part riddle: "What is the room you leave without entering?" and "What is the room you enter without leaving?" I told him I had no use for riddles, so he left.
That's the fellow who does my laundry.
I heard somebody lifted that Egyptian pigsticker from the museum. Word on the street says it was an inside job.
New York is the place to be. All kinds come through here--a real melting pot. There's even a high-class international con man in town, but I cannot tell you who. He would kill me if he found out.
That's where my pal Crodfoller works.
Ah...I believe he's a policeman.
Never heard the name before, toots.
Do I look like an encyclopedia? I know nothing about it.
That's the fellow who found the fancy pigsticker in Egypt.
What makes you think I know anything about police stations? You take me for a hood? I have friends in high places, toots. Very high places.
That's the museum accountant. A quiet, high-hat sort of fellow.
You mean this speakeasy? Best in town. I know because I have visited all the competition.
The name rings a bell. I believe he works on the docks.
That's me. Were you planning to make something of it?
Do not touch me, toots.
Who sent you?
Crodfoller? He's an old pal of mine. What do you want to know?
You mean The Sun Also Rises, his novel of postwar disillusion? Naturally. Ernest and I go way back. He ran it by me before publication, and I told him it was a corker.
I do not talk to strangers, toots.
I have not got all day to shoot the breeze. Do you have a specific question?
Never heard of them, toots. Amscray.
A compact, carefully dressed man whose large, nervous eyes never seem to rest.
